candidate.selection_reason: User-controlled path input -> resolve() instead of normalize() -> changes path resolution security behavior
candidate.source_summary: User-provided path parameter passed to root() method
candidate.sink_summary: File system operations via path.join(root, path) and path.normalize() in pipe() method
candidate.guard_summary: Path validation: null byte check, malicious path check (path.substr(0, root.length) !== root), dotfile handling, upPathRegexp for '..' detection
candidate.risk_pattern: User-controlled path resolved to absolute path then joined with user-controlled path parameter, with boundary checks that may be bypassed through path traversal sequences
enclosing_conditions: if (root !== null) branch in pipe() method
candidate.context_summary: The root() method sets _root using path.resolve(), which converts relative paths to absolute. In pipe(), this resolved root is joined with user-controlled path and normalized, with security checks for path traversal.
unresolved_facts: Whether path.resolve() behavior differs significantly from path.normalize() in security context
Specific attack scenarios that could bypass the existing path validation checks

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
target_cwe.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory. Common in: path_traversal, input_validation.
target_cwe.impact: code execution, data access, data modification
remediation_steps: Validate and sanitize all file paths and names
Use canonical path resolution and access controls
